newsitem.title: USA: WHX raises Dynamics bid to $45/shr.
newsitem.headline: WHX raises Dynamics bid to $45/shr.

text.p: WHX Corp, parent of Wheeling-Pittsburgh Steel Corp, said Wednesday it had raised its unsolicited takeover bid for Dynamics Corp of America to $45 a share from $40.
The higher offer comes nine days after directors of Dynamics, a diversified electronic components maker, said they considered the original WHX bid "totally inadequate."
WHX reiterated that the number of shares it was targeting in the first stage of its takeover attempt was 649,000, or 17.0 percent of Dynamics's outstanding shares.
When added to its current stake of 2.9 percent, WHX said it would end up with a 19.9 percent holding in Dynamics.
It said the price it will pay for the remaining shares in the second stage of its merger proposal was also $45 a share.
WHX said a valid tender will no longer require the tendering stockholder to be a record holder as of March 14 or otherwise hold an irrevocable proxy from a record holder as of that date.
WHX said it believes its new $45-a-share bid represents an "attractive" price for Dynamics.
It said it was willing to negotiate a friendly merger "and thereby avoid the necessity of a proxy contest for corporate control."

However, it said that as it previously announced, it plans to solicit proxies for Dynamics' annual meeting, scheduled for May 2, to elect four of its nominees to Dynamics's board and amend by-laws of the company.
WHX reiterated that it has no plans to increase the ownership stake of 44.1 percent held by Dynamics in CTS Corp, an electronics and electro-mechanical components manufacturer.
